page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m1.2xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, supported by a 33 MB L3 cache. The instance is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or a GPU, and operates on a KVM hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results position this instance in the average tier for most CPU and memory operations. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core tests yield scores of 1856.99 and 7723.84 respectively, while the Geekbench multi-core score reaches 5272.0. Memory bandwidth tests show 59.61 GB/sec for large block read-only operations. However, the server exhibits performance limitations in memory-bound and complex workloads. Redis SET operations are weak at 7.86 million operations per second, and medium-sized 7B LLM inference prompt processing is poor at 15.97 tokens per second.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.u1-c1m1.2xlarge is its highly constrained memory capacity of 1.0 GB per vCPU and the complete lack of local storage. This hardware profile provides a cost-efficient option for compute-centric workloads that do not demand significant memory footprints or local disk space. It is suitable for tasks such as light software compilation, static web serving, basic text processing, and small-scale model inference.
